tagline.text: A cable wakeboard park beneath Mount Isarog, among Asia's best known

location.label: Location
location.text: Inside the Provincial Capitol Complex, Cadlan, Pili, Camarines Sur

children.text: Camsur Watersports Complex (CWC) is a cable wakeboard park inside the Provincial Capitol Complex in Pili, Camarines Sur. It opened in 2006, has hosted several world-level competitions, and draws everyone from first-timers to pros with a beginner cable and on-site lodging.

Camsur Watersports Complex is usually shortened to CWC. It sits inside the Provincial Capitol Complex in Cadlan, Pili, in Camarines Sur in the Bicol region. The name makes many people assume it is in Naga City, but administratively it is in Pili. Naga Airport is also in Pili, so the airport is close, which is a big plus. Riders launching into the air over a wide lake, with Mount Isarog in the distance, is the park's signature scene.

The core facility is the cable park. Instead of a boat pulling riders, an electric cable system strung over the lake does the towing, so there is little engine noise and several people can ride back to back without a boat. CWC is known to use a six-point cable system with six towers, and each lap offers obstacles for practicing jumps and rail tricks. Many travel accounts also agree that there is a separate beginner cable for first-timers and a pro cable where athletes train.

As for history, CWC opened in 2006 and is described as having hosted international events such as the World Wakeboarding Championships and an IWWF World Cup. Local media reported that the 2016 Wake Park World Championship drew riders from more than 20 countries. The big lake was once temporarily closed for renovation, and cabins were badly damaged by Typhoon Nina in December 2016, so the condition of the facilities has varied over time. In 2024 a wakeboard magazine described a resurgence of the park along with plans for new facilities.

There are reasons to visit even if you do not wakeboard. The Villa del Rey lodging area, a watersports pro shop, and dining are all in one place, and you can also try water skiing, kneeboarding, and wakeskating. It suits anyone who wants to add a day or two of active fun to a Bicol trip. However, hours, rates, and which areas are open change often, so check the latest information with the booking desk or official channels before you go. For first-timers, a typical day goes like this: buy a pass, rent gear, and start by practicing standing up on the beginner cable. The cable pulls riders at a steady speed, so no boat driver is needed to match your pace. The key is keeping your center of gravity low through each lap, and after a few falls you get the hang of it. It is tiring, so rest well at lunch, and be careful not to swallow lake water.

An electric cable circling six towers pulls riders around the lake. Several people can ride in turn without a boat, and the obstacle sections let you practice jumps and rail tricks, which is why the park is described as one of the best in the world. With no boat noise, it is easy to chat on the shore, and spectators can watch riders' lines up close.
A separate cable is set aside for first-timers. The slower speed and simpler layout make it good for learning balance. Helmets and life vests can be rented.
A pro cable draws Filipino and overseas riders to train. Even if you do not ride, you can watch advanced tricks up close from the shore.

CWC has hosted the 2016 Wake Park World Championship, the World Wakeboarding Championships, and an IWWF World Cup. When events overlap your dates, spectators and athletes crowd the park, so check the schedule in advance.
Besides wakeboarding, water skiing, kneeboarding, and wakeskating are said to be available. Check on site which activities are offered and what they cost.
Lodging on site ranges from budget cabins and cabanas to upscale villas. You can sleep right next to the lake and start riding early in the morning, which is very convenient.
Local reports say an inflatable aqua park was added after storm damage. Companions or children who do not wakeboard can spend time at the water play area.
Arrive when the park opens, buy a pass at the desk, and rent a helmet, life vest, and board. Confirm that day's open areas.
Take a basic lesson on the beginner cable and practice standing up. Most people fall a lot in the first hour, so start relaxed.
Have lunch at an on-site restaurant and rest. Your arms will be sore, so do not overdo it.
Ride again in an afternoon session or watch the pros from the shore.
Pack up and head out. Check on site whether night sessions run.
Starting early lets you avoid the midday heat and leaves time for shaded rest.
Arrive at Naga Airport, check in at Villa del Rey, and warm up gently on the beginner cable in the afternoon.
Ride all day and add one skill at a time. In the evening, eat Bicol dishes in central Naga or at the on-site restaurant.
Ride one more morning session and check out. If time allows, look around Naga City's churches and markets.

In January 2026 the Camarines Sur tourism site promoted a package with two nights in a cabana, unlimited wakeboarding, golf, and more. Confirm the validity period and conditions with the booking desk.
Whether there are domestic flights from Manila to Naga Airport (WNP) varies by period, so check airline announcements.
Naga Airport is in Pili, close to CWC. Take a tricycle or taxi from the airport.
Airport transfers are sometimes included in packages, so ask your lodging.
On days without flights, you can also fly into Legazpi Airport and continue overland.
Take a long-distance bus from Manila toward Naga and get off in Pili. Plan on an overnight bus usually taking eight hours or more.
Get off at the gate of the Pili Provincial Capitol Complex and walk into the complex.
Timetables and fares differ by company, so check before you leave.
From Naga City to Pili is a short trip by jeepney, van, or taxi.
Get off at the entrance of the Capitol Complex and ask at the complex information desk how to reach the lake inside.
Rain can slow your trip.

Cable wakeboarding is done on a lake, so it depends less on sea conditions, but heavy rain and typhoons can halt operations or damage facilities. Bicol has no clear dry season and rains often even in winter, so be sure to check the forecast.

March to early June is comparatively clear and good for riding, and because midday heat is strong, morning and late-afternoon sessions are more comfortable. Prepare for typhoon season toward the end of the year.

The closest lodging is Villa del Rey inside the complex. It is known to offer everything from budget cabins, cabanas, and container rooms to upscale villas, so you can choose to suit your group and budget. Sleeping beside the lake means you can ride at first light, which is the biggest advantage. Rooms fill quickly in peak season and during competitions, so book ahead. You can inquire with the official booking desk by email or phone.

For meals you can use the on-site restaurant and pro shop, and if you have time, head into Naga City to try Bicol cuisine. Bicol food is famous for coconut milk and chili, so tell the kitchen in advance if you cannot handle spice.

For groups or families, it is easiest to ask about gear rental, transfers, and meals all at once when booking lodging. If someone in your party does not ride, they can watch from the shore or spend time at the water play area. Bicol portions are generous, so start with a light lunch.
If it is your first time, start on the beginner cable and ask for lessons or help.
Always wear a helmet and life vest, and check the rental deposit and the rules on lost gear.
A rash guard or long-sleeved top protects against scrapes from falls and against sunburn.
Secure sunglasses and hats with a strap or leave them behind. They are hard to find once they fall in the water.
Starting early means fewer people and weaker sun, which is good for practice.
Bring a waterproof pouch or case, and leave valuables at your lodging.
Confirm the day's open areas and whether night sessions run at the desk after you arrive.
Muscle soreness is common, so do not ride too long on the first day, and schedule rests.
Take care not to swallow lake water, and shower and clean any cuts after riding.
Bicol is a typhoon-prone region. Check the forecast and CWC announcements before you leave, and follow safety rules.
Some rates in this guide are from 2012 and may differ from today's, so be sure to confirm on site.
Wakeboarding easily injures arms, shoulders, and knees. Check your travel insurance.
Do not ride after drinking alcohol.
Operating hours and open lakes can change because of maintenance or events.
Keep an eye on your belongings and cash while traveling.
Night operations and lighting vary by period, so confirm beforehand.

A large religious festival held in Naga that you can add to your itinerary if the timing fits. Lodging gets very crowded, so book early.
